title_en: Regulations on the National Agricultural Census

articles.content_en: These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Statistics Law of the People's Republic of China for the purpose of organizing and implementing the national agricultural census scientifically and effectively, and ensuring the accuracy and timeliness of agricultural census data.

The purpose of the agricultural census is to comprehensively grasp the basic situation of agriculture, rural areas, and farmers in China, to provide a basis for researching and formulating economic and social development strategies, plans, policies, and scientific decision-making, and to provide statistical information services for agricultural producers and operators and the public.

The agricultural census work shall be organized and implemented in accordance with the principles of unified national leadership, division of labor and cooperation among departments, and hierarchical responsibility at local levels.

State organs, social organizations, and units and individuals related to the agricultural census shall, in accordance with the Statistics Law of the People's Republic of China and these Regulations, actively participate in and closely cooperate with the agricultural census work.

Agricultural census leading group offices at all levels (hereinafter referred to as census offices) and their staff, census supervisors, and enumerators (hereinafter collectively referred to as census personnel) shall independently exercise the powers of investigation, reporting, and supervision according to law, and no unit or individual shall interfere.
Leaders of various localities, departments, and units shall not modify the agricultural census data lawfully provided by census offices and census personnel on their own, shall not compel or instruct census offices, census personnel, or census respondents to falsify agricultural census data or fabricate false data, and shall not retaliate against persons who refuse or resist the falsification of agricultural census data or the fabrication of false data.

Publicity departments at all levels shall make full use of media such as newspapers, radio, television, the Internet, and outdoor advertising, adopt various forms, and earnestly carry out the publicity and mobilization work for the agricultural census.

The funds required for the agricultural census shall be jointly borne by the Central and local people's governments at all levels, included in the fiscal budgets of the corresponding years, and allocated on time to ensure full availability.
The agricultural census funds shall be uniformly managed, used only for designated purposes, and expenditures shall be strictly controlled.

The agricultural census shall be conducted once every 10 years, with years ending in the digit 6 as census years, and the standard reference time shall be 24:00 on December 31 of the census year. The census registration time in special regions may be appropriately adjusted with the approval of the Office of the Leading Group for the Agricultural Census of the State Council.

Agricultural census respondents shall truthfully answer the inquiries of census personnel, fill in the agricultural census forms on time, and shall not make false reports, conceal reports, refuse reports, or delay reports.
Agricultural census respondents shall cooperate with the supervision and inspection lawfully conducted by the statistical institutions of the people's governments at or above the county level and the survey teams dispatched by the National Bureau of Statistics, truthfully reflect the situation, provide relevant materials, and shall not refuse, prevaricate, or obstruct the inspection, and shall not transfer, conceal, tamper with, or destroy original records, statistical ledgers, census forms, accounting materials, and other relevant materials.
The industry scope of the agricultural census includes: crop cultivation, forestry, animal husbandry, fishery, and services for agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry, and fishery.

The contents of the agricultural census include: agricultural production conditions, agricultural production and operation activities, agricultural land use, rural labor force and employment, rural infrastructure, rural social services, farmers' livelihood, and the circumstances of townships, villagers' committees, and community environment, etc.
The agricultural census contents specified in the preceding paragraph may be adjusted by the Office of the Leading Group for the Agricultural Census of the State Council according to specific circumstances.

The agricultural census shall adopt the method of comprehensive survey. The Office of the Leading Group for the Agricultural Census of the State Council may decide to adopt the method of sample survey for specific contents.
The agricultural census shall adopt the national statistical classification standards.

The agricultural census plan shall be uniformly formulated by the Office of the Leading Group for the Agricultural Census of the State Council.
Provincial census offices may, as needed, add supplementary tables for the agricultural census, and implement them after submitting them to the Office of the Leading Group for the Agricultural Census of the State Council for approval.

The State Council shall establish a leading group for the agricultural census and its office. The Leading Group for the Agricultural Census of the State Council shall be responsible for organizing and leading the national agricultural census work. The Office of the Leading Group for the Agricultural Census of the State Council shall be located in the National Bureau of Statistics and shall be specifically responsible for the organization and coordination of the daily work of the agricultural census.

Local people's governments at all levels shall establish leading groups for the agricultural census and their offices, and shall be responsible for the organization and implementation of the agricultural census within their respective administrative regions in accordance with the unified provisions and requirements of the Leading Group for the Agricultural Census of the State Council and its office. The survey teams dispatched by the National Bureau of Statistics shall, as member units of the leading groups for the agricultural census and their offices, participate in the organization and implementation of the agricultural census.
Villagers' committees shall, under the guidance of township people's governments, do a good job in the agricultural census within their respective areas.

Relevant departments of the State Council and local people's governments at all levels shall actively participate in and closely cooperate with the census offices in carrying out the agricultural census work.
The agricultural census work of agricultural production units under the armed forces and the armed police forces shall be organized and implemented by the armed forces and the armed police forces respectively.
The agricultural census work of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps shall be organized and implemented by the leading group for the agricultural census of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps and its office.

The on-site registration of the agricultural census in rural areas shall be conducted by census areas. Census areas shall be divided on the basis of the management territories of villagers' committees, and each census area may be divided into several enumeration districts.
The on-site registration of the agricultural census in urban areas shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of the census plan.

Each enumeration district shall be equipped with one enumerator, responsible for the interview and registration work of the census. Each census area shall be equipped with at least one census supervisor, responsible for arranging, guiding, and supervising the work of the enumerators, and may also conduct direct interview and registration.
Census supervisors and enumerators shall be mainly composed of village and township cadres, leaders of villagers' groups, and other local residents with a relatively high level of education.
Census supervisors and enumerators shall be in good health and have a strong sense of responsibility.

Census offices may, based on work needs, employ or second personnel from other relevant units to engage in agricultural census work. Relevant units shall actively recommend qualified personnel to engage in agricultural census work.
Employed personnel shall have their labor remuneration paid by the employing unit. The salaries of seconded personnel shall be paid by their original units, and their welfare benefits shall remain unchanged.
Appropriate work subsidies shall be arranged in the agricultural census funds for village census supervisors and enumerators.

Local census offices shall provide professional training to census supervisors and enumerators, and shall issue nationally unified census supervisor certificates or enumerator certificates to those who have passed the assessments.

Census personnel shall have the right to inquire of relevant units and individuals about matters related to the agricultural census, and request that such units and individuals truthfully provide relevant information and materials, and correct untruthful materials.

Census personnel shall adhere to the principle of seeking truth from facts, abide by professional ethics, and refuse and resist illegal acts in the agricultural census work.
Census personnel shall strictly implement the census plan, and shall not forge or tamper with census data, and shall not compel or instruct census respondents to provide false census data.
When carrying out agricultural census tasks, census supervisors and enumerators shall present the census supervisor certificate or enumerator certificate.

Enumerators shall, according to law, directly visit the census respondents, conduct inquiries and fill in the forms on the spot. After the census forms are completed, they shall be confirmed by the signature or seal of the census respondent. The census respondent shall be responsible for the authenticity of the census data he or she has signed or sealed.
Census personnel shall be responsible for the consistency of the census data they are responsible for registering, reviewing, and entering with the census data signed or sealed by the census respondent.
Census offices shall be responsible for the accuracy of the census data they process and compile.

The data processing plan and implementation measures for the agricultural census shall be formulated by the Office of the Leading Group for the Agricultural Census of the State Council.
Local census offices shall carry out data processing in accordance with the provisions of the data processing plan and implementation measures, and shall report the census data on time.
The data processing work of the agricultural census shall be organized and implemented by the census offices at or above the level of a city divided into districts.

Census offices shall do a good job in data backup and loading into the database, establish and improve the agricultural census database system, and strengthen routine management and maintenance updates.

The State shall establish a quality control system for agricultural census data.
Census offices shall implement quality control and inspection acceptance for each link in the implementation of the census.

Census personnel shall implement a responsibility system for quality control work.
Census personnel shall review, recheck, and accept census data in accordance with the provisions of the census plan.

The Office of the Leading Group for the Agricultural Census of the State Council shall uniformly organize the post-enumeration quality check of agricultural census data. The results of the spot checks shall serve as an important basis for evaluating the quality of agricultural census data of the whole country or of each province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.

The State shall establish a system for the publication of agricultural census data.
Summary data of the agricultural census shall be promptly published to the public, except for those kept confidential according to law.
The national agricultural census data and the main agricultural census data of each province, autonomous region, and municipality directly under the Central Government shall be reviewed and approved by the Office of the Leading Group for the Agricultural Census of the State Council and published jointly with the relevant departments of the State Council.
When local census offices issue census bulletins, they shall report to the census office at the next higher level for approval.

Census offices and census personnel shall keep confidential the data of individual census respondents collected in the agricultural census work, and shall not use them for purposes other than the census.

Census offices shall do a good job in the preservation, management, and provision of services to the public regarding agricultural census data, and shall develop and apply the agricultural census data.

The statistical institutions of the people's governments at or above the county level and relevant departments may, based on the results of the agricultural census, revise the historical data of relevant routine statistics. The specific measures shall be formulated by the National Bureau of Statistics.
Units and individuals that earnestly implement these Regulations, are devoted to their duties, adhere to principles, and have made outstanding achievements shall be given awards.

Where leaders of localities, departments, or units modify agricultural census data on their own, compel or instruct census offices, census personnel, or census respondents to tamper with agricultural census data or fabricate false data, or retaliate against persons who refuse or resist tampering with agricultural census data or refuse or resist fabricating false data, they shall be given administrative sanctions or disciplinary sanctions according to law, and shall be given a notice of criticism by the statistical institution of the people's government at or above the county level or the survey team dispatched by the National Bureau of Statistics; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Where census personnel fail to implement the census plan, forge or tamper with census data, or compel or instruct census respondents to provide false census data, the statistical institution of the people's government at or above the county level or the survey team dispatched by the National Bureau of Statistics shall order corrections, give administrative sanctions or disciplinary sanctions according to law, and may also give a notice of criticism.

Where census personnel are derelict of duty or commit malfeasance causing serious consequences, they shall be given administrative sanctions or disciplinary sanctions according to law, and may also be given a notice of criticism by the statistical institution of the people's government at or above the county level or the survey team dispatched by the National Bureau of Statistics.

Census offices shall set up reporting telephone numbers and mailboxes to accept reports and supervision from all sectors of society regarding illegal acts in the agricultural census, and shall give awards to persons who have rendered meritorious services in reporting.
These Regulations shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
